The most likely explanation is that Glenn gave up his password or had it trapped by a keylogger or other government surveillance software. The FBI has tried to crack TrueCrypt's encryption before and had no luck.

So what I understand from the article, is this isn't likely huge news like the click-bait title suggests?

If there turns out to be evidence that TrueCrypt was in fact cracked (unlikely, AES256 is pretty much uncrackable from my understanding, and bruteforcing a key would take billions of years on average if I recall correctly) then this probably needs more attention and TrueCrypt needs to make some sort of announcement to it's remaining users. Just because it's been discontinued does not mean that everyone has switched, as there is still widespread belief that it is secure.

The TrueCrypt group DID say to stop using it. But they did several weird things long with their announcement:

  1. Released a "patched" version of the software.
  2. Removed their warrant canary.
  3. Made the ridiculous suggestion to switch to Bitlocker.

http://truecrypt.sourceforge.net/

So it's not that people in the know have been saying to use TrueCrypt... they've been specifying to use 7.1a, not 7.2, since the latter could actually be compromised.

Well, 7.1a a group of people crowdfunded a professional audit for. It was part of the process to help "prove" to the public that, as downloaded from the sourceforge site, the package was secure and could be trusted for encryption. Releasing a new version would undo the work people were putting into that.

"warrant" is the wrong word; they had a statement at the bottom of the page, a "canary" like the concept of "a canary in a coal mine" that people were instructed that, if the message ever disappeared, that means that they were compromised in some way by an intelligence agency.

Bitlocker is Windows' own encryption solution that, I believe, it's been covered that MS keeps a back door to the encryption for.

7.1a may still be okay, but I wouldn't trust 7.2 or anything disseminating from that site for anything life and death.
